section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a study involving 369 women that aimed to clarify the effects of cognitive fusion and body appreciation on the relationship between perceived body-ideal discrepancy and disordered eating behavior, while controlling for BMI. The results indicated that women perceiving a significant discrepancy between their real and idealized body tend to exhibit more disordered eating behaviors. This relationship is partially explained by higher levels of cognitive fusion regarding physical appearance and lower body appreciation.
